gappers.catalyst: Nebius shares fell premarket as AI-cloud growth-story risks build and peer CoreWeave also drops on AI-safety-driven infrastructure-spending fears.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius (NBIS) is extending a slide Benzinga describes as "stuck in a bear market" this morning — despite strong revenue growth, investors are focused on risks to the growth story including heavy cash burn (FCF TTM -$5.88B, capex TTM -$11.14B) funded by debt/equity raises (debt/equity ~1.0x, $7.5B in LT debt issued TTM). Premarket weakness is compounded by a sector-wide AI-safety scare: headlines this morning tie an OpenAI/Anthropic AI-safety-litigation appeal to a broad AI-trade selloff (NVDA, MU, SNDK, ORCL, TSLA also named), and peer CoreWeave (CRWV) is down ~8% premarket on the same AI-infrastructure-spending-fear narrative.
gappers.why: No NBIS-specific event (no earnings, no guidance change) — this is a sentiment/positioning-driven de-rating: AI-safety-litigation headlines are pulling risk out of high-multiple AI-infrastructure names broadly, and NBIS (21% short interest, ~46x forward P/S) is a high-beta target for that unwind.
gappers.impact: Alpaca premarket volume of 390K is a small fraction of the 20.75M average daily volume — not yet high-conviction distribution. Move reads as macro/sector-fear driven rather than NBIS-specific, so it could fade if the AI-safety headline cools, but the stock was already technically weak (confirmed bear market, RSI 45) so further breakdown is also plausible. CoreWeave dropping in sympathy confirms sector-wide AI-infra rotation, not an NBIS-only story.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM - no structural catalyst (M&A, contract win, guidance reset); this is a risk-off move tied to an active news cycle and should mean-revert or extend with the broader tape rather than anchor a multi-week thesis.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Zero open positions currently (confirmed via TRADE-LOG/account), so no existing holding is displaced. Moot regardless: this strategy is long-bias only per standing rule (gap-down names are excluded the same as every prior session) and NBIS gapped DOWN -10.2%, so it is not an eligible long candidate at any R:R — watchlist-only, no trade angle here.

gappers.catalyst: Oracle extends its post-earnings slide after founder Larry Ellison filed to sell $7.5B in shares, compounding a broader AI-safety-driven selloff in AI infrastructure names.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Oracle (ORCL) reported Q1 FY2027 earnings Thursday Sep 10 after the close; the stock has slid from $150.28 (Sep 10 close) to $143.04 premarket today. Benzinga reports founder Larry Ellison has filed to sell shares worth $7.5B, reviving downside risk after an earlier report that he had canceled a similar 50M-share sale following the strong print. Today's drop also coincides with a market-wide AI-safety scare (OpenAI/Anthropic appeals rattling the AI trade) that Benzinga names ORCL among the stocks in focus for, alongside NVDA, MU, SNDK, TSLA. Not all coverage is negative: one analyst (Jeff Kilburg) called Oracle's AI-cloud position "essential" even as the stock dips.
gappers.why: Two stacked pressures: (1) company-specific — Ellison's $7.5B share-sale filing signals insider supply hitting the market right after earnings, and (2) sector-wide — the same AI-safety headline cycle hitting NBIS/CRWV/NVDA is pressuring high-capex AI-infrastructure names broadly, and Oracle's own capex/FCF profile (capex TTM -$55.66B, FCF TTM -$23.69B, debt/equity 2.3x) makes it a natural target for that de-rating.
gappers.impact: Premarket volume 1.55M vs a 32.8M average daily volume — elevated for premarket but not yet a print that confirms capitulation-level distribution. This reads as a continuation of the post-earnings fade (3 sessions now) rather than a one-day headline spike, given the stacked insider-selling and sector-fear catalysts; sustainability depends on whether Ellison's filing actually executes and whether the AI-safety headlines keep pressuring the group.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM - the immediate driver (insider-sale filing + AI-safety headline fear) is not a durable structural catalyst; however this is worth re-checking post-open since the underlying Q1 FY2027 earnings were reported strong (per the earlier Ellison-cancellation piece) - if the tape stabilizes this could re-open as a LONG_TERM dip-buy candidate on a later /trade check, not today.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Zero open positions currently, so no existing holding is displaced. Not an eligible long candidate today regardless: this strategy is long-bias only (gap-down names excluded per standing rule) and ORCL gapped DOWN -6.6% — watchlist-only for now; would need to clear the Entry Checklist confluence and 2:1 R:R on a subsequent bounce/stabilization before consideration.
